newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-GKN sees 18 mln stg hit on profit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GKN sees 18 mln stg hit on profit.

text.p: GKN Plc, the UK engineering giant, said sterling's relentless rise against European currencies is likely to have a serious impact on 1997 results, with its chief executive predicting that it may take a minimum of 18 million stg off operating profits.

CK Chow, GKN chief executive, told Reuters in an interview that most of stg's gains had been made in the second half of last year and that stg stood 12 percent higher at the 1996 year-end compared with its year average. "Every one percent move by stg against the European currencies means 1.5 million (stg) off operating profits for GKN." That totals at 18 million even before accounting for sterling's rise since December 31.
On December 31, the British currency was trading around 2.63 Deutsche marks, compared to 2.23 marks in January 1996. It is currently even higher at 2.76 marks.
Chow said the impact on last year's operating profit was 5.2 million stg describing the situation this year as "more serious."
But despite the currency impact, which is not hedged for translation effects, Chow expects 1997 to be a year of progress.
In the automotive business, he said growth would be fuelled by a mix of productivity growth, new products and gains in emerging markets. Those markets include Poland, China and Korea.
Productivity gains will come from the U.S. and Italy where the group is seeking to turnaround performance.

Commenting on the on-going litigation process against its U.S. franchise operation Meineke Discount Muffler Shops, which is still awaiting final judgement, Chow said the group had not made any provision in the results so far because there was no decision on a possible award to Meineke.
He said the group had a strong case for appealing if it did go against them.

GKN said in a statement on February 20 it expected the award to be 30 percent lower than originally feared. Earlier that month it had feared the damages could top $740 million. GKN has cash reserves of 528 million stg.
The cheif executive did not believe that the threat of a legal award eating into cash reserves would hinder GKN's chances of making acquisitions or seeking alliances.
Chow said he aimed to identify growth platforms for possible deals, naming aerospace structures and components and agri-technical construction and vehicle components in particular.
He said the group was looking for opportunities but added that nothing was imminent.

Commenting on the outlook for the aerospace and defence businesses, he said completion of the major Warrior armoured vehicle contract for Kuwait in the second half of 1997 would not impact this year, but be felt in 1998.
The group still has a major contract to supply 67 GKN Westland Apache helicopters, with deliveries running through to 2003.
Industrial services will launch some new products this year but the benefit will start to be felt the year after, he said.
